Thanks Eric — good, concrete questions. I reviewed your redlines and prepared a proposal with three pragmatic options so procurement/legal can pick a path that balances predictability and flexibility: see attached RWI_MSA_proposed_redline.docx. Summary below: 

Option A — Short notice, customer-friendly (most flexible)
- Auto-renew disabled by default; explicit renewal required by Customer OR customer must provide written election 30 days prior to term end
- Notice window for termination: 30 days
- TFC allowed by either party with no fee, Redwood provides 30 days of transition support

Option B — Balanced compromise (recommended)
- Single automatic renewal for a 12-month term unless Customer opts out 60 days prior to term end by providing written notice
- Notice window for termination for convenience: 60 days
- TFC permitted by either party; Redwood provides transition support up to 60 days; early termination triggers pro-rated refund of prepaid usage credits excluding consumed committed capacity

Option C — Enterprise predictability (Redwood preferred)
- Auto-renew for subsequent 12-month terms unless Customer gives 90 days notice
- Termination for convenience allowed only after initial 12-month commitment with a 90-day notice; early offboards incur an offboarding fee equal to 15% of remaining committed fees or Redwood-provided migration assistance, at Customer election

Implementation notes:
- Billing impact: pro-rata refunds handled as credit applied to future invoices. For pre-paid annual commitments, we propose an audit to confirm consumed tokens.
- Operational: we can add a renewal reminder email 75/45/15 days out (configurable) and a one-click opt-out in the Billing Console.

Would you prefer we preserve your redline language verbatim in the attached docx and annotate our counter, or produce a clean final that reflects Option B (our recommendation) for signature?

Best,
